facts.statement: Redondasuchus is an extinct genus of aetosaur.
facts.quote: Redondasuchus is an extinct genus of aetosaur.

facts.statement: Fossils of Redondasuchus have been found in the Redonda Formation in east-central New Mexico.
facts.quote: Material belonging to the genus has been found from the Redonda Formation in east-central New Mexico.

facts.statement: The type species R. reseri was named in 1991, though it had previously been classified as a species of Typothorax since 1985.
facts.quote: The type species, R. reseri, was named in 1991 after having been referred to as a species of Typothorax since 1985.

facts.statement: A second species, R. rineharti, was described in 2006.
facts.quote: A second species, R. rineharti, was described in 2006.

facts.statement: The type species R. reseri was named based on isolated scutes found at Apache Canyon and Shark Tooth Hill in Quay County, New Mexico.
facts.quote: R. reseri was named on the basis of isolated scutes found at Apache Canyon and Shark Tooth Hill in Quay County, New Mexico.

facts.statement: Unlike other aetosaurs with radially patterned scutes, Redondasuchus scutes are densely pitted but lack any specific patterning.
facts.quote: While other aetosaurs have scutes covered in pits and grooves that often form radial patterns, the scutes of Redondasuchus are densely covered in pits and lack any patterning.

facts.statement: The dorsal paramedian scutes of Redondasuchus are unique because they are angled approximately 45 degrees.
facts.quote: The dorsal paramedian scutes (those that line the back) are unique in that they are angled approximately 45°.

facts.statement: In both Redondasuchus species, each paramedian scute has an underside keel extending from the medial edge to the flexed area.
facts.quote: In both species, each paramedian possesses a keel on the underside that extends from the medial edge (the edge near the vertebrae) to the flexed area of the scute.

facts.statement: Jeffrey Martz suggested that R. reseri is synonymous with Typothorax coccinarum, a hypothesis that remains debated.
facts.quote: Martz also suggested that R. reseri was synonymous with Typothorax coccinarum.

facts.statement: An independent investigation by the Society of Vertebrate Paleontology found no evidence of explicit, intentional plagiarism in the 2006 paper describing Redondasuchus.
facts.quote: A separate independent investigation by the Society of Vertebrate Paleontology did not find evidence for explicit, intentional plagiarism in Spielmann et al. (2006).

facts.statement: Heckert et al. (1996) classified Redondasuchus as part of an advanced grade of aetosaurs alongside Neoaetosauroides, Longosuchus, Desmatosuchus, Paratypothorax, and Typothorax.
facts.quote: Heckert et al. (1996) considered Redondasuchus to be part of an advanced grade of aetosaurs that also included Neoaetosauroides, Longosuchus, Desmatosuchus, Paratypothorax, and Typothorax.

facts.statement: Redondasuchus is classified within the family Stagonolepididae.
Redondasuchus lived between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago during the Norian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)
